title: Javascript ES6 Destructuring Challenge Solution
summary: Walkthrough of the cars destructuring challenge: unpack the array into honda and tesla, then dig into each object for the renamed top speed and the first colour. Each added line removes one more undefined-variable error from the table code.

concepts.heading: Step 1: import and inspect the data
points: practice.js needs a default export of cars; the app file imports it below the other imports.
Logging cars first shows an array of two objects with nested objects and arrays, similar to a real API response.
Working out which variable names the (unchangeable) table code expects tells you what to create: honda, tesla, hondaTopSpeed, teslaTopSpeed, hondaTopColour, teslaTopColour.

concepts.heading: Step 2: destructure the array
points: const [honda, tesla] = cars; assigns item 0 and item 1 by position.
This alone makes honda.model and tesla.model resolve, so the model column renders and the related errors disappear.
honda now holds the whole Honda Civic object.

concepts.heading: Step 3: nested object for top speed
points: topSpeed sits inside the speedStats object, so destructure speedStats from honda and open a second pair of braces after a colon to reach inside it.
Inside, pick topSpeed and rename it with another colon, e.g. topSpeed: hondaTopSpeed. zeroToSixty can be pulled out in the same braces too, though the table does not use it.
Repeat for tesla with teslaTopSpeed. The top speed column now fills in for both rows.
(Extra) If zeroToSixty is destructured from both cars without renaming, the second const zeroToSixty clashes with the first; rename one (zeroToSixty: teslaZeroToSixty) or leave it out.

concepts.heading: Step 4: nested array for top colour
points: coloursByPopularity is an array, so after the colon use square brackets: coloursByPopularity: [hondaTopColour] takes the first element and names it.
Same again for tesla. The table now shows black for Honda and red for Tesla.

(Extra) The walkthrough builds the speed and colour patterns as separate statements; the reference repo merges them into one statement per car, which works because a single object pattern may mix array and object sub-patterns.

concepts.heading: Rule of thumb
points: Mirror the shape of the data in the pattern: braces where the data is an object, brackets where it is an array, a colon to step one level deeper or to rename.

task.name: Solution to the cars destructuring challenge
task.starting_point: The previous lecture's sandbox with the challenge table code uncommented and practice.js holding the cars array.
task.goal: Make the table render model, top speed and top colour for both cars purely by adding destructuring.
steps: Confirm practice.js ends with export default cars; and import it in the app file: import cars from "./practice";
console.log(cars) to inspect the nesting, and list the variable names the table code uses (honda, tesla, hondaTopSpeed, teslaTopSpeed, hondaTopColour, teslaTopColour).
Destructure [honda, tesla] from cars; the model column now renders.
Destructure speedStats: { topSpeed: hondaTopSpeed } from honda and the same with teslaTopSpeed from tesla; the top speed column fills in.
Destructure coloursByPopularity: [hondaTopColour] from honda and coloursByPopularity: [teslaTopColour] from tesla; the colour column fills in.
Optionally merge each car's two patterns into a single const statement.
task.expected_result: Table rows show Tesla Model 3 / 150 / red and Honda Civic / 140 / black with no undefined-variable errors.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 36 - React.js/36.31 Javascript ES6 Object & Array Destructuring/es6-destructuring/src/App.jsx

pitfalls: Forgetting the colon-then-braces (or brackets) means you get the nested object itself, not the inner value.
Names must match the keys exactly (coloursByPopularity, British spelling) or the result is undefined.
Do not edit the provided table code; create the variables it expects.

playground.coverage: No playground lesson yet (playground data covers only sections 1-11, 14, 15).
gaps_and_ideas: Add as the final task of the proposed Destructuring lesson: starter code gives a cars array (model, coloursByPopularity, speedStats) and a rendered table that references hondaTopSpeed, teslaTopColour etc.; the learner writes only the destructuring lines, and a checker compares each variable's value with the expected one.

Demo idea: a shape-mirroring visual: show the data object as a tree and highlight, as the learner hovers each part of the pattern ({ }, [ ], colon), which node of the data it grabs and what variable name it creates.
